messages:
maya: Heads up — planning to add a new column `service_tier` (values: 'free'|'paid') to telemetry.events so console quotas + per-route billing can avoid expensive joins. Want migration plan + UX for rollouts.

oliver: Quick Q — why denormalize onto events instead of keeping a route_tiers table? joins are cheap in analytics cluster.

maya: Main reasons: 1) reduce realtime join cost in console dashboards, 2) make routing/limits decisions cheaper in Dedicated path, 3) avoid repeated lookups in hot paths. But worried about storage + backfill cost.

li: If we add it nullable first we can shadow-write from control plane then backfill. But nullable enums explode query plans in some of our materialized views.

sam: Proposal: phased approach — (A) add nullable column with no default, (B) start dual-write from control plane behind feature flag, (C) run idempotent backfill jobs that populate historical rows in batches, (D) switch queries to prefer denorm column with compatibility fallback, (E) drop join path after one or two releases. Thoughts? :+1: :thinking_face:

oliver: Sounds reasonable. Two safety calls: 1) backfill should be rate-limited and monitor bytes/sec, 2) dashboards need experiment & canary so we don't regress query latencies.

maya: Agreed. Also need to decide enum enforcement: DB CHECK vs application-level. CHECK constraint prevents typos but blocks dual-write until all writers updated. Might do app-level validation + nightly schema migration to add CHECK later.

sam: For backfill, here's a sketch of batch SQL we'll run in housekeeping cluster (postgres):

```sql
BEGIN;
UPDATE telemetry.events e
SET service_tier = r.tier
FROM route_metadata r
WHERE e.route_id = r.route_id
  AND e.service_tier IS NULL
  AND e.ts >= now() - interval '180 days'
  AND e.id IN (SELECT id FROM telemetry.events WHERE service_tier IS NULL LIMIT 10000 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED);
COMMIT;
```

li: Prefer to do the batch by partition (date) instead of LIMIT to avoid scanning hot partitions. Also record progress in a migration table so retries are safe.

devbot: [schema-migration] job scheduled: telemetry.service_tier.backfill v1 queued by @sam — job_id=job-8342

maya: UX: console routes page should continue to derive quota if service_tier is NULL by calling route metadata API. When we flip the flag, prefer column. Add a per-route migration status indicator in console so support can see which routes still missing tier.

eva: Dashboard callouts: need to update a couple Grafana panels that do `count by route` which currently join to route metadata. Need a compatibility layer in the metrics exporter for ~2 weeks to emit both old and new metrics until consumers migrate.

sam: Agree. We'll produce both metrics for a short window. Also alert thresholds: backfill job >10MB/sec for 5m should pause and notify infra.

oliver: Query plan check — add an explain/capture step in CI for top 5 dashboard queries against a small snapshot with the new column populated (and nullable) so we can detect plan regressions early.

li: One more: consider adding a `service_tier_v2` with explicit versioning if we think the enum might expand later. Minimizes migration pain when values change.

maya: Good call. If we do v2 we'd keep v1 as compatibility until console deprecates. But let's not overcomplicate unless product expects more tiers.

sam: Action items:
- sam: create dual-write feature flag + SDK changes (this week)
- li: migration table + partitioned backfill runner (next week)
- oliver: CI explain harness for dashboard queries (this sprint)
- maya: console UX changes + per-route migration indicator (design by EOD)
- eva: metric exporter compatibility PR (before backfill)

maya: I'll draft a runbook for the backfill pause thresholds + rollback steps. Putting a canary on a single org first.

oliver: If canary looks good, we should window the full backfill during off-peak hours and ensure we have snapshot + restore point before starting.

maya: Sounds good. Thanks all.

eva: ping when the compatibility exporter PR is ready — I'll update dashboards after that.

sam: job-8342 started (dry-run) — will post logs here when first batch completes.

devbot: [schema-migration] job job-8342 state=RUNNING dry_run=true

maya: Filing the migration RFC in the repo now with the plan above and the rollback checklist. Will link here in a bit.

sam: first dry-run batch finished: 10k rows scanned, 4.1MB updated, no errors. attaching short log snippet.

maya: Nice. If dry-run stays clean we'll flip dual-write next.
